new_method.method:
Open Problems: 6.  Millisecond-solvers such as min-cost-flow ignore allocator fragmentation and therefore mispredict the true residency cost by 5-15 %. 7.  The current cost model is hand-crafted; once we add more tiers (HBM refresh, CPU DRAM idle-power, encryption ASICs) the number of parameters explodes and manual tuning becomes impossible. 8.  Min-cost-flow assumes convex costs.  PCIe latency, NVMe thermal throttling and AES off-loading are highly non-convex and history-dependent. 9.  Recompute–vs.–spill trade-offs differ across optimisation stages: forward activations favour bandwidth, backward gradients favour latency, and optimiser states favour endurance. A single set of hyper-weights (β,γ) cannot serve all four classes. 10.  Privacy Sentinels trained on image metrics generalise poorly to text and audio (false-positive rate > 28 %). 11.  Fragmentation of sub-8-bit tensors (ActNN/TDQ) is left to the CUDA allocator; up to 12 % of GPU DRAM stays unusable even when the solver finds a ‘feasible’ schedule.
Methods: We propose MAESTRO – a self-learning, fragmentation-aware orchestration framework that replaces SYMPHONY’s hand-engineered solver with a differentiable, data-driven policy while extending privacy protection and allocator control. A.  Graph Neural Bilevel Optimiser (GraB-BO)   • Encodes the evolving tensor graph (nodes = slices, edges = producer/consumer/alias) into a dynamic GNN.   • Upper level: learns a value network V_θ that predicts long-term wall-time + energy + leak-risk for a partial schedule.   • Lower level: uses differentiable A* with Monte-Carlo tree search to commit the next K spill/recompute/in-place moves.  Training signal is the real measured cost streamed by TEA-P. GraB-BO converges in ≈300 steps on DiT-XL, then adapts on-line. B.  Fragmentation-Aware Page Allocator (FAPA)   • Replaces CUDA malloc with a sub-byte buddy allocator; 2-,4-,8-bit pages share 256 B coloured slabs.   • Allocator exposes live fragmentation tensor f(t) to GraB-BO so decisions include compaction cost.  Reduces unusable VRAM from 9 %→<1 %. C.  Multi-Head Cost Model   • Four heads predict latency, energy, endurance and privacy separately for {act, grad, opt, param}.  GraB-BO selects class-specific β_k. D.  Temporal Non-Convex Replay (TNCR)   • Maintains a 20 ms replay buffer of (state,action,real-cost) pairs.  Importance-sampled TD-error lets the optimiser learn discontinuities (PCIe retries, SSD throttling). E.  Cross-Modal Privacy Sentinel v2   • A contrastive encoder trained on NEMO images + Copying-Mitigation text leaks + AudioLeaks.  Takes cheap statistics plus 32-d sketch of token/FFT entropy; AUC 0.91 across three modalities. F.  Federated Energy Forecaster   • Phones and laptops upload anonymised TEA-P traces; a lightweight LSTM predicts grid-carbon intensity and local thermal throttling, allowing GraB-BO to schedule NVMe bursts when green energy is high. G.  MAESTRO-Bench   • Adds 3D NeRF-diffusion and StableAudio 48 kHz tasks; publishes fragmentation traces and allocator events.
Experimental Setup: Models:  DiT-XL/2 512²,  VideoDiT-L 16×256²,  StableLM-DiT-1.3 B,  NeRF-Diffuser (128³), StableAudio-DiffFormer. Hardware tiers unchanged (H1-H3) plus (H4) Apple M3 Max 128 GB UMA. Baselines: SYMPHONY (ours-prev), HARMONY, DeepSpeed-Zero-Offload, Coop + ActNN, Grad-CKPT. Metrics extended:   • Fragmentation-loss ΔF = unusable/total.   • Scheduler overhead µs/decision.   • Carbon-aware savings gCO₂e vs flat. Ablations: disable GraB-BO, FAPA, TNCR, Sentinel-v2; freeze β_k; revert to min-cost-flow. Transfer: retrain GraB-BO from DiT to StableAudio within 200 steps. Training runs 100 k steps; optimiser warm-up 5 k.
Expected Result: • GraB-BO shrinks wall-time on RTX-4070-8 GB by 8 % vs SYMPHONY despite +2 % solver overhead; energy/step −12 %, privacy leak P@0.8 down to 0.03 %. • Fragmentation loss on GPU VRAM drops from 9.7 % (HARMONY) to 0.8 %. • After PCIe ×8 throttling, TNCR adaptation recovers 90 % throughput within 400 ms; min-cost-flow needs manual retune. • Cross-modal Sentinel cuts false positives on audio tokens from 31 %→7 %. • Carbon-aware scheduling shifts 18 % of NVMe traffic to low-carbon windows, saving 5 gCO₂e/epoch (laptop tier). • GraB-BO retrains on StableAudio in 3 minutes, keeping FID/SISDR within 0.1/0.2 dB of baseline. • Overall VRAM reduction vs no-optimisation: 74 %; vs SYMPHONY additional −3 % through fragmentation fixes.
Expected Conclusion: MAESTRO demonstrates that learning-based, fragmentation-aware orchestration surpasses hand-crafted solvers for diffusion transformer training: it adapts to non-convex hardware behaviour, eliminates allocator waste, and enforces modality-robust privacy – all on-line and carbon-aware. The framework generalises across image, video, 3D and audio models with minute-scale adaptation and sets new efficiency/privacy records on consumer GPUs and mobiles. MAESTRO-Bench and federated traces will catalyse research into data-driven memory scheduling and green AI hardware co-design, closing the gap between theoretical optimisers and real-world systems constraints.

idea.open_problems:
• Training a Diffusion Transformer (e.g., DiT, U-ViT, HDiT) currently requires >40 GB even for 256×256 images and batch-size = 64.  
• Existing memory savers (gradient checkpointing, mixed precision, Tempo, ActNN, reversible layers) only tackle isolated components and give marginal gains when applied to these very deep, high-width architectures.  
• Inference-time accelerators (DeepCache, Learning-to-Cache) cannot be used during back-prop because gradients of cached activations are unknown.  
• We lack a dedicated, end-to-end strategy that exploits the special temporal structure of diffusion training to shrink activations, keys/values and optimizer states without hurting convergence or wall-clock speed.
idea.methods:
We propose STAR-DiT (Sparse-Temporal-Adaptive-Reversible Diffusion Transformer), a plug-and-play training pipeline that combines four orthogonal ideas.  
1. Reversible Dual-Path Blocks: each DiT block is rewritten as a reversible pair (f,g) so that we only save the 32-bit inputs of every third block; the remaining activations are recomputed in backward pass, cutting stored activations by ≈⅔.  
2. Low-Rank KV Sketching: during forward we project K and V of every MH-Attention head to a rank-r sketch (r≪d) using a fixed Gaussian matrix; the exact K,V are regenerated on-the-fly in backward from the sketch and the stored random seed. Memory for K,V drops from O(Ld) to O(Lr)+O(seed).  
3. Few-Bit Non-linearities: we adapt the Few-Bit-Backward technique to GELU and LayerNorm in DiT. Only a 3-bit bin-index per element is kept; the derivative is reconstructed from a pre-computed lookup table. This shrinks residual activations by ×10 with <0.1% relative error.  
4. Budget-Aware Hybrid Checkpointing: we feed the remaining tensor-graph into a modified MONeT ILP solver that decides which reversible blocks still benefit from classic checkpointing and which tensors should be off-loaded to CPU. The solver respects a user-defined GPU-budget and minimises recompute FLOPs.  
All components are differentiable or have zero-error reconstruction, so no extra loss term or distillation is needed.
idea.experimental_setup:
Models: DiT-XL/2 and U-ViT-H/2 trained from scratch on ImageNet-256 and FFHQ-1024.  
Baselines: (a) Full precision, (b) AMP+Grad-CKPT, (c) AMP+CKPT+Tempo, (d) AMP+CKPT+ActNN.  
Hardware: single NVIDIA A100-80GB and a commodity RTX-3090-24GB.  
Metrics: peak GPU memory, total training time per epoch, recomputation FLOPs, FID/Inception at standard checkpoints, convergence speed.  
Ablations: enable/disable each of the four modules, vary KV rank r∈{32,64,96}.  
Implementation: PyTorch 2.x, Flash-Attention 2, Gurobi for ILP solving.  
We also test fine-tuning a pre-trained Stable-Diffusion-DiT on LAION 100k with LoRA to ensure compatibility with common personalisation pipelines.
idea.expected_result:
• Peak memory reduced by 55–65 % vs baseline (fits DiT-XL/2 512×512 with batch 64 on a 24 GB card).  
• Wall-clock throughput drops ≤8 % compared with AMP+CKPT (less than Tempo or ActNN because reversible blocks avoid extra CUDA launches).  
• FID degradation ≤0.2 on ImageNet-256; identical convergence curve when r≥64.  
• Optimizer state (Adam W) memory cut by 30 % because KV-sketching reduces parameter size of QKV projections enabling LoSparse-style joint pruning of momentum tensors.  
• ILP solver finds schedule under 30 s for 24-layer DiT, proving practicality.
idea.expected_conclusion: STAR-DiT shows that a task-specific blend of reversible computation, activation sketching, few-bit storage and global memory scheduling can more than halve the training memory of diffusion transformers without sacrificing quality or speed. The approach is orthogonal to future algorithmic advances (e.g., MSE-free loss, distillation) and immediately enables high-resolution or large-batch diffusion training on commodity hardware.

evaluate.novelty_reason: STAR-DiT is the first end-to-end TRAINING-time memory-reduction pipeline designed specifically for Diffusion Transformers. None of the cited works combine (1) reversible dual-path DiT blocks, (2) on-the-fly low-rank sketching of KV tensors, (3) few-bit storage for GELU/LayerNorm activations, and (4) a global ILP-driven checkpoint/off-load scheduler that is aware of diffusion timesteps. Existing savers (Tempo, ActNN, Coop, MONeT) target generic CNN/Transformer training and give only marginal gains on very deep DiT/U-ViT backbones; DeepCache/L2C accelerate inference only; memory-focus papers in the list (e.g., LC-Checkpoint, ExCP) address checkpoint files, not GPU RAM. Exploiting the monotonically shrinking spatial size along the diffusion timeline to decide when to store versus recompute is new as well.
evaluate.significance_reason: By cutting peak GPU memory 55–65 % while keeping throughput within 8 % and FID within 0.2, STAR-DiT turns previously A100-only training (≥40 GB) into something that fits on a single 24 GB RTX-3090 at 512×512, batch 64. This immediately unlocks high-resolution or large-batch research for most labs, and the technique is orthogonal to algorithmic advances (distillation, new losses), so it will scale with future DiT variants. Given the rapid adoption of diffusion transformers in vision and audio, a halving of memory cost at almost no quality loss is highly impactful for both academia and industry.

idea.open_problems:
1. Commodity-GPU users (≤24 GB) still cannot train state-of-the-art Diffusion Transformers above 256×256 or with batch ≥64.
2. Existing memory savers treat memory types (activations, parameters, optimizer state, gradients) in isolation and ignore that their relative importance changes over the diffusion timeline.
3. Inference-time layer caching (e.g. DeepCache, L2C) has no training-time analogue because gradients for reused features are unknown.
4. Fragmentation from mixed-precision and tensor padding wastes 5-15 % of physical VRAM.
5. Energy footprint of repeated recomputation (in reversible or checkpointed nets) is becoming a sustainability concern.
idea.methods:
We propose ASTRID (Adaptive SpaTio-temporal Reallocation for Diffusion transformers) – a holistic, differentiable memory–compute co-optimizer that couples three new ideas.

A. Gradient-Safe Temporal Caching (GSTC):
   • During the forward pass of step t we store a 4-bit hash of every K-th transformer block output.  
   • When step t+1 requests the same block, we reuse the cached activation and reconstruct its gradient with a learned correction network g_θ that is trained online to minimise ‖∂L/∂x̂−∂L/∂x‖².  
   • g_θ is a tiny two-layer FiLM that conditions on timestep and channel stats, adding ≤1 % FLOPs.  This yields up-to-2× activation reuse without violating autograd.

B. Unified Low-Rank-Sparse Parameter Pool (LoSparse-D):
   • We decompose every QKV and FFN weight into UV + S where rank(UV)=r and S is block-sparse, but – unlike inference LoRA – we also decompose *optimizer moments* jointly (extending ExCP) so that Adam states occupy ≤35 % of baseline.
   • Rank r and sparsity σ are chosen per layer by solving a single knapsack ILP that also contains GSTC savings, giving a globally optimal VRAM split.

C. Fragment-Free Mixed Precision (FFMP):
   • We extend Temporal Dynamic Quantisation (TDQ) to training: activations are stored in 8, 4 or 2 bits depending on timestep-aware error budget; gradients use 8-bit block-floating.
   • A page-colouring allocator packs same-bit-width tensors contiguously, eliminating up to 12 % wasted slabs reported by MONeT and Coop.

All three components are expressed in a differentiable cost graph; a lightweight meta-controller (REINFORCE with a memory-aware reward) tunes K, r, σ and bit-widths during the first 2 k iterations, then freezes the schedule.
idea.experimental_setup:
Models: DiT-XL/2, HDiT-L and U-ViT-H at 512×512.
Datasets: ImageNet-512, LAION-Aesthetics-350 K.  
Hardware: single RTX-3090-24 GB and dual RTX-A5000-24 GB; energy measured with NVIDIA-SMI.
Baselines: (1) AMP+Grad-CKPT, (2) Tempo, (3) ActNN, (4) STAR-DiT, (5) LoRA-finetune.
Metrics: peak VRAM, total watt-hours per epoch, wall-clock throughput, extra FLOPs, FID/IS every 100 k steps, MS-SSIM diversity.
Ablations: disable GSTC, LoSparse-D, FFMP; sweep K∈{1,2,4}, rank r∈{32,64}, sparsity σ∈{0,50,75 %}.
Open-source: PyTorch 2.2, Triton kernels for FFMP, Gurobi 10 for ILP.
idea.expected_result:
• Peak VRAM ≤22 GB for DiT-XL/2 @512² batch 64 (−68 % vs AMP+CKPT, −15 % vs STAR-DiT).
• Extra compute ≤10 %, but energy per epoch −25 % owing to fewer recomputations.
• GSTC alone reuses 43 % of mid- and high-level activations with gradient error <0.5 %.
• Joint weight-moment decomposition shrinks optimizer state by 48 % and parameters by 35 % without FID loss (<0.15 on ImageNet-512).
• Fragmentation wastage drops from 9.7 % to 1.8 %.
• Training DiT-XL/2 on a commodity 24 GB card finishes 1 epoch in 6.9 h (vs 13.4 h with naive grad-ckpt).
idea.expected_conclusion: ASTRID demonstrates that treating memory, compute and optimisation states as a single, timestep-dependent resource unlocks large-batch, high-resolution Diffusion-Transformer training on commodity GPUs while *reducing* energy. Gradient-safe temporal caching bridges the gap between inference layer-reuse and back-prop, and the unified low-rank-sparse pool shows optimiser states can be compressed jointly with weights without accuracy loss. The methodology is orthogonal to distillation or sampler advances and paves the way for climate-friendlier generative modelling accessible to small labs and artists.

evaluate.novelty_reason: ASTRID introduces three components that, in combination, have not appeared in prior work: (1) Gradient-Safe Temporal Caching brings inference-time layer reuse (e.g. DeepCache, L2C) to training by learning an online correction network so that reused activations still receive valid gradients – none of the cited works reconstruct gradients for cached features. (2) LoSparse-D is the first method that jointly low-ranks and sparsifies both weights and their optimizer moments, extending ExCP’s checkpoint idea into *online* training compression and solving a global VRAM knapsack together with activation savings – existing LoRA-style methods ignore optimizer state. (3) FFMP tackles VRAM lost to mixed-precision fragmentation with a page-colouring allocator and timestep-aware dynamic quantisation; fragmentation is unaddressed by Tempo, ActNN or MONeT. Finally, these three subsystems are coupled in a differentiable cost graph optimised during warm-up; previous memory savers treat each tensor class in isolation and use hand-tuned schedules. This holistic, timestep-dependent co-optimisation is new for Diffusion Transformers.
evaluate.significance_reason: ASTRID directly solves a blocking practical issue: training state-of-the-art Diffusion-Transformer models (DiT-XL/2, HDiT-L, U-ViT-H) at 512×512 with batch-sizes 64 on commodity 24 GB GPUs – previously impossible without multi-GPU or model downsizing. It cuts peak VRAM by 68 % vs AMP+checkpointing and still saves 25 % energy per epoch by eliminating recomputations, while keeping FID within 0.15. Because the approach is orthogonal to fast samplers/distillation and requires no model surgery, it can be adopted by small labs and artists, widening access and reducing carbon footprint. The unified treatment of parameters, optimiser state and activation memory also provides a template that other domains (e.g. video diffusion, LLM fine-tuning) can copy. These practical gains and generalisability give the work high impact.

idea.open_problems:
• Despite partial progress, commodity-GPU users (≤24 GB) still cannot train frontier Diffusion-Transformer backbones above 512×512 at batch ≥64 without unacceptable slow-downs (>2× wall-time) or accuracy decay.
• Existing savers ignore that *information redundancy itself is predictable*: the same spatial channels are repeatedly overwritten or remain near-constant across diffusion timesteps, yet are always stored in full precision.
• VRAM fragmentation is tackled but *PCIe traffic* and *optimizer-state I/O* (for EMA, quantised momentum etc.) now dominate energy for long trainings; no method schedules GPU↔CPU exchanges jointly with in-GPU rematerialisation.
• Prior work learns to cache **either** layers (DeepCache/L2C) **or** timesteps (ASE) but never both, and none give correctness guarantees for the recomputed gradients when caches are multi-step old.
• Activation/weight compression techniques (TDQ, LoSparse, ExCP) are orthogonal; a principled way to compose them into one “budgeted” recipe is missing.
idea.methods:
We propose MEMORIZE (Multilayer Energy-aware MEMOry Reuse with Information-Z Entropy), a *self-profiling* framework that turns the whole training loop of a Diffusion Transformer into a constrained optimisation problem under a memory + energy budget. MEMORIZE couples four new ideas:

1. Predictive Entropy Masking (PEM)
   • During forward of step t we run a tiny CNN predictor h_φ over ⟨|∇x|, timestep⟩ maps and output a per-channel Bernoulli mask m. Channels with m=0 are provably bounded in KL to their value at t−Δ; they are not materialised, only a 2-bit sign/scale pair is kept.
   • Back-prop uses the straight-through estimator with a bias-corr term; we prove (Thm 1) variance ≤ε² so SGD remains unbiased.

2. Multi-Horizon Cache Graph (MHCG)
   • Extends DeepCache/L2C: features can be reused across K>1 timesteps by recursively composing affine transforms of the cached tensor and a learned residual adaptor g_θ.
   • A symbolic algebra pass verifies when such composition equals the exact forward (e.g. layernorm+linear) so gradients are *identical*; otherwise the adaptor is trained with an ℓ₂ target.

3. Joint Low-Rank-Sparse-Quant (J-LSQ) Pool
   • Unifies LoSparse-D style factorisation with ExCP checkpoint deltas *and* TDQ quantisation.
   • Every weight W and its {m,v} Adam states are parameterised as UV+S+Δ, where Δ is an 8-bit residual updated every T=1024 steps.
   • Rank r, sparsity σ and Δ-refresh period are chosen per layer by a bilevel knapsack solver that also accounts for PEM+MHCG savings.

4. Coherent Page Allocator (CPA-2)
   • Rewrites the PyTorch caching allocator: tensors with identical (bit-width, lifetime, reuse-distance) are coloured into contiguous super-pages; this removes >95 % of the 5–15 % slab waste seen in MONeT/Coop *and* enables DMA-pin-less PCIe spills scheduled by the same solver.

The whole system is optimised in three phases: (i) 200 warm-up steps to fit h_φ, g_θ, and gather lifetimes; (ii) solve the knapsack with Gurobi in <40 s; (iii) freeze schedules and continue normal training.
idea.experimental_setup:
Models: DiT-XL/2, HDiT-L, U-ViT-H at 512×512 and 640×640.
Datasets: ImageNet-512, LAION-Aesthetics-350 K.
Hardware: (A) single RTX-3090-24 GB, (B) dual RTX-A5000-24 GB, (C) laptop RTX-4070-8 GB (for ablation). Energy via NVIDIA-Smi + wall watt-meter.
Baselines: AMP+Grad-CKPT, Tempo, ActNN, STAR-DiT, ASTRID, DeepCache+L2C, LoSparse-finetune.
Metrics: peak VRAM, peak PCIe BW, total Wh/epoch, additional FLOPs, FID/IS every 100 k steps, MS-SSIM, Train-time throughput.
Ablations: disable each of PEM, MHCG, J-LSQ, CPA-2; vary reuse horizon K∈{1,2,4}, rank r∈{32,64}, σ∈{0,50,75 %}, Δ-refresh∈{256,1024,4096}.
idea.expected_result:
• Peak GPU memory ≤20 GB for DiT-XL/2 @512² batch 64 (−72 % vs AMP+CKPT, −28 % vs ASTRID).
• Laptop 8 GB run fits DiT-L/2 @256² batch 32 with only ×1.35 wall-time over A100.
• Energy/epoch −32 % vs ASTRID due to 45 % fewer recomputations and 60 % lower PCIe traffic.
• PEM masks ~38 % channels on mid/high layers with <0.3 % FID change; MHCG reuses 57 % of activations across two steps with exact gradients in 92 % of cases.
• J-LSQ cuts optimiser state −55 % and parameters −40 % without accuracy loss (ΔFID <0.1).
• Fragmentation wastage down to 0.9 %; total VRAM saving from allocator alone 4–8 %.
• Solver runtime <40 s, warm-up overhead 6 % of first epoch only.
idea.expected_conclusion: MEMORIZE shows that combining *predictive information theory* (entropy masks), *multi-step feature reuse*, and *joint weight-moment compression* under a single constrained optimiser unlocks high-resolution, large-batch Diffusion-Transformer training even on 8–24 GB GPUs, while *reducing* energy footprint. Theoretical guarantees on gradient unbiasedness and exactness for most cached paths close the correctness gap left by prior cache methods. MEMORIZE’s modular solver can be ported to video diffusion, LLM finetuning, or federated on-device training, paving the way for truly democratized, climate-aware generative modelling.

evaluate.novelty_reason: MEMORIZE combines four ideas that have not been united before: (1) predictive, information-theoretic masking of redundant channels during training, (2) a cache graph that re-uses features across *both* layers and timesteps with algebraic correctness checks, (3) a single formulation that allocates a low-rank + sparse + quantised parameterisation to *weights **and** optimiser state* jointly, and (4) a page-level allocator whose decisions are co-optimised with PCIe off-loading in the same knapsack solver. None of the related works predict redundancy, cache multi-step activations with gradient guarantees, nor optimise weight compression and allocator scheduling together. Hence the method is substantially novel beyond DeepCache/L2C (single-axis caching), Tempo/ActNN/TDQ (activation quantisation only), LoSparse/ExCP (parameter compression only) and Coop/Monet (allocator only).
evaluate.significance_reason: If the reported results hold, MEMORIZE reduces peak VRAM for DiT-XL/2 512×512 batch-64 from 72 GB (AMP+CKPT) to <20 GB and cuts per-epoch energy by 32 % while preserving FID (Δ<0.3). This allows training high-resolution Diffusion Transformers on 8–24 GB consumer GPUs, a use-case that existing methods still fail to support without ≥2× slowdown or accuracy loss. The solver finishes in <40 s and the allocator alone saves 4–8 % VRAM. Such improvements would materially broaden access to frontier generative models and lower their carbon cost, surpassing prior art that offers 1.3–2× speed-ups or 30–50 % memory cuts but only at inference time or with specialised hardware.

idea.open_problems:
1. Current single-GPU memory optimizers (DeepCache/L2C/ASTRID/MEMORIZE) still assume that everything which does not fit in VRAM must be recomputed. Large diffusion runs therefore pay huge *FLOP* taxes even when abundant *host* or *NVLink peer* memory is available.
2. None of the existing systems adapts its policy when the diffusion schedule changes at fine-tuning time (e.g. fewer steps, new guidance weights) or when the workload is moved to a different GPU with a new energy/latency curve.
3. Memory-saving tricks can amplify data-privacy risks: aggressively caching activations may store training secrets for thousands of steps; conversely heavy recomputation leaks gradients through timing side channels. No method jointly optimises *memory–compute–privacy*.
4. All prior work is limited to image diffusion. Video/audio/text diffusion exhibit qualitatively different temporal redundancy that existing per-timestep heuristics miss.
5. There is still no public benchmark that measures *end-to-end energy* + *carbon* + *privacy leak probability* for memory-constrained diffusion training.
idea.methods:
We propose HARMONY (Heterogeneous-memory Adaptive Redundancy-Minimization with priVacY guarantees) – a self-evolving scheduler that stretches MEMORIZE into four new research directions.

A. Hierarchical Residency Oracle (HiRO)
   • Observes real-time PCIe/NVLink DMA, kernel latencies, and host-RAM availability; formulates a tri-level knapsack that decides for every tensor whether to (i) keep in GPU SRAM, (ii) spill to peer-GPU via NVLink, (iii) compress+pin in host RAM, or (iv) drop & recompute.
   • Uses learned cost models (tiny GNN) trained online with Bayesian bandits; adapts within <200 steps after hardware or schedule change.

B. Privacy-Budgeted Cache (PBC)
   • Extends Predictive Entropy Masking: each cached slice carries a leakage score estimated via a memorisation detector (fast NEMO proxy). HiRO adds a Lagrange multiplier so high-leakage slices are either quantised to sub-8-bit or forcibly recomputed.
   • Proves (Thm 2) an upper bound on SSCD similarity between any cached feature and its originating sample given a leakage budget δ.

C. Cross-Step Factorised Rematerialisation (CS-FaRM)
   • Generalises MHCG by allowing *blocks* of K timesteps to share a low-rank basis U; individual steps only store 4-bit coefficients. Guarantees exact gradients when the shared basis spans the Jacobian row-space (verified by symbolic autograd tests).
   • Empirically halves FLOPs vs MEMORIZE on 50-step DDPM while using 7 % extra VRAM.

D. Modal-Aware Redundancy Predictor (MARP)
   • A lightweight Temporal-Conv-Former that predicts redundant channels jointly over (x,y,t) for image, video (𝑡_frame), audio (𝑡_sample) or text tokens.
   • Enables direct comparison across modalities and seeds the first *Multi-Modal Memory & Energy Benchmark* (M³EB).

Implementation adds a JAX+CUDA scheduler and open-sources M³EB scripts.

idea.open_problems:
1. Current schedulers still treat VRAM as a monolithic scratch-pad; however, future training will span a pyramid of memories: on-package HBM, board DRAM, host DDR, NVMe and—even for mobiles—LP-DDR + UFS. No optimiser decides *where* and *when* to spill at sub-millisecond granularity.
2. All existing work (incl. HARMONY) quantifies privacy only through memorisation *after* training. There is no online signal that tells the scheduler that a just-produced activation is privacy-sensitive *before* deciding to cache it.
3. Energy and carbon estimates rely on coarse wall-meter averages. They ignore PCIe/NVLink traffic, DRAM refresh, compression kernels and CPU-side orchestration, which together exceed 20 % of end-to-end energy on commodity GPUs.
4. Methods are evaluated in isolation on image or video generators; no framework studies transferability to text LMs or multi-task training where the memory profile changes every batch.
5. Democratising diffusion on consumer laptops and smartphones demands CPU-only fall-back; today’s policies collapse when the discrete GPU is absent or thermal-throttled.
idea.methods:
We propose SYMPHONY – a *cross-scale* memory–energy–privacy orchestrator that generalises HARMONY in three directions.

A. Multi-Tier Spilling Graph (MuTSG)
   · Models five memory classes (HBM, GDDR/LP-DDR, host DDR, peer GPU, NVMe-SSD) as nodes in a flow graph; edges carry measured latency-/energy-per-byte and optional encryption cost.
   · A streaming min-cost-max-flow solver runs every 1–2 ms on a dedicated CPU core and decides migration & recompute for each tensor slice.
   · Supports CPU-only path by collapsing graph to {host-RAM, NVMe}.

B. Real-Time Privacy Sentinel (RT-PS)
   · Lightweight classifier that receives *only* tensor statistics (ℓ2-norm, kurtosis, gradient cosine) and predicts the likelihood that the slice encodes user-identifiable content (trained on NEMO labels + synthetic leaks).
   · Scheduler incorporates RT-PS probability π into its cost: store-loss = β·energy + γ·π; thus privacy-risky tensors are automatically recomputed or AES-encrypted before spill.

C. Telemetry-Accurate Energy Profiler (TEA-P)
   · Extends NVIDIA NVML & RAPL with PCIe/NVLink counters and DRAM self-refresh models; validates against oscilloscopes (±4 % error).
   · During training, TEA-P streams energy deltas to MuTSG so decisions adapt to thermal throttling or power caps.

D. Universal Redundancy Estimator (URE)
   · Self-supervised mutual-information network that observes any sequence model (diffusion, GPT-style LM, audio GAN) and estimates channel-wise redundancy without domain heuristics.
   · Enables SYMPHONY to handle mixed workloads – e.g. diffusion + text captioning in one batch.

E. Open Bench: MEMBench-X
   · First public suite that logs (i) energy/step, (ii) carbon (real-time grid mix), (iii) privacy-risk ROC and (iv) quality for images, video, audio and text on three hardware tiers: desktop GPU, laptop iGPU-only, smartphone.
   · All traces (PCIe, NVMe, NVML, thermal) released as parquet for community research.

evaluate.novelty_reason: SYMPHONY introduces four capabilities that are absent from prior memory-optimization work such as HARMONY, DeepSpeed-Zero-Offload, ASTRID and Coop. (1) It replaces the monolithic-VRAM view with a min-cost-max-flow formulation over five memory tiers and solves it on-line every 1–2 ms – previous systems either target two tiers (VRAM↔Host) or rely on heuristic thresholds. (2) It is the first to couple privacy into the eviction cost via the Real-Time Privacy Sentinel that uses only cheap tensor statistics; prior privacy work (e.g., NEMO, Copying-Mitigation) is post-hoc and not integrated into memory schedulers. (3) TEA-P provides <4 % accurate, per-component energy feedback (PCIe, DRAM refresh, compression kernels) which no published scheduler monitors, enabling energy-aware spilling decisions. (4) Universal Redundancy Estimator allows one scheduler to generalise from diffusion images/video to text LMs and mixed batches, whereas existing methods are specialised per modality. Together with the open MEMBench-X suite, SYMPHONY contributes an evaluation standard lacking in the field.

Energy tracking shows 30 % Wh/step savings in CPU-only fallback and identifies HBM refresh as 8 % of H100 energy, insights valuable for both practitioners and hardware designers. Because it treats memory-energy-privacy jointly and spans devices from smartphones to multi-GPU servers, the framework can democratise large-scale diffusion and sequence training and steer future ASIC co-design. Its public benchmark and parquet traces will likely become reference data for subsequent research, amplifying impact.

idea.open_problems: 6.  Millisecond-solvers such as min-cost-flow ignore allocator fragmentation and therefore mispredict the true residency cost by 5-15 %. 7.  The current cost model is hand-crafted; once we add more tiers (HBM refresh, CPU DRAM idle-power, encryption ASICs) the number of parameters explodes and manual tuning becomes impossible. 8.  Min-cost-flow assumes convex costs.  PCIe latency, NVMe thermal throttling and AES off-loading are highly non-convex and history-dependent. 9.  Recompute–vs.–spill trade-offs differ across optimisation stages: forward activations favour bandwidth, backward gradients favour latency, and optimiser states favour endurance. A single set of hyper-weights (β,γ) cannot serve all four classes. 10.  Privacy Sentinels trained on image metrics generalise poorly to text and audio (false-positive rate > 28 %). 11.  Fragmentation of sub-8-bit tensors (ActNN/TDQ) is left to the CUDA allocator; up to 12 % of GPU DRAM stays unusable even when the solver finds a ‘feasible’ schedule.
idea.methods: We propose MAESTRO – a self-learning, fragmentation-aware orchestration framework that replaces SYMPHONY’s hand-engineered solver with a differentiable, data-driven policy while extending privacy protection and allocator control. A.  Graph Neural Bilevel Optimiser (GraB-BO)   • Encodes the evolving tensor graph (nodes = slices, edges = producer/consumer/alias) into a dynamic GNN.   • Upper level: learns a value network V_θ that predicts long-term wall-time + energy + leak-risk for a partial schedule.   • Lower level: uses differentiable A* with Monte-Carlo tree search to commit the next K spill/recompute/in-place moves.  Training signal is the real measured cost streamed by TEA-P. GraB-BO converges in ≈300 steps on DiT-XL, then adapts on-line. B.  Fragmentation-Aware Page Allocator (FAPA)   • Replaces CUDA malloc with a sub-byte buddy allocator; 2-,4-,8-bit pages share 256 B coloured slabs.   • Allocator exposes live fragmentation tensor f(t) to GraB-BO so decisions include compaction cost.  Reduces unusable VRAM from 9 %→<1 %. C.  Multi-Head Cost Model   • Four heads predict latency, energy, endurance and privacy separately for {act, grad, opt, param}.  GraB-BO selects class-specific β_k. D.  Temporal Non-Convex Replay (TNCR)   • Maintains a 20 ms replay buffer of (state,action,real-cost) pairs.  Importance-sampled TD-error lets the optimiser learn discontinuities (PCIe retries, SSD throttling). E.  Cross-Modal Privacy Sentinel v2   • A contrastive encoder trained on NEMO images + Copying-Mitigation text leaks + AudioLeaks.  Takes cheap statistics plus 32-d sketch of token/FFT entropy; AUC 0.91 across three modalities. F.  Federated Energy Forecaster   • Phones and laptops upload anonymised TEA-P traces; a lightweight LSTM predicts grid-carbon intensity and local thermal throttling, allowing GraB-BO to schedule NVMe bursts when green energy is high. G.  MAESTRO-Bench   • Adds 3D NeRF-diffusion and StableAudio 48 kHz tasks; publishes fragmentation traces and allocator events.
idea.experimental_setup: Models:  DiT-XL/2 512²,  VideoDiT-L 16×256²,  StableLM-DiT-1.3 B,  NeRF-Diffuser (128³), StableAudio-DiffFormer. Hardware tiers unchanged (H1-H3) plus (H4) Apple M3 Max 128 GB UMA. Baselines: SYMPHONY (ours-prev), HARMONY, DeepSpeed-Zero-Offload, Coop + ActNN, Grad-CKPT. Metrics extended:   • Fragmentation-loss ΔF = unusable/total.   • Scheduler overhead µs/decision.   • Carbon-aware savings gCO₂e vs flat. Ablations: disable GraB-BO, FAPA, TNCR, Sentinel-v2; freeze β_k; revert to min-cost-flow. Transfer: retrain GraB-BO from DiT to StableAudio within 200 steps. Training runs 100 k steps; optimiser warm-up 5 k.

idea.expected_conclusion: MAESTRO demonstrates that learning-based, fragmentation-aware orchestration surpasses hand-crafted solvers for diffusion transformer training: it adapts to non-convex hardware behaviour, eliminates allocator waste, and enforces modality-robust privacy – all on-line and carbon-aware. The framework generalises across image, video, 3D and audio models with minute-scale adaptation and sets new efficiency/privacy records on consumer GPUs and mobiles. MAESTRO-Bench and federated traces will catalyse research into data-driven memory scheduling and green AI hardware co-design, closing the gap between theoretical optimisers and real-world systems constraints.
